propositions.text: I dismiss this appeal.
propositions.quote: I dismiss this appeal.

propositions.text: The Appellant is a citizen of Uganda who fears the Government of Uganda and their security apparatus.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX (Appellant) is a citizen of Uganda. 1. The Appellant fears the Government of Uganda and their security apparatus.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges he is sought by government authorities because he was a former supporter of the Democratic Party and current supporter of the National Unity Platform.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that he is sought out by government authorities because he is a former supporter of the Democratic Party (DP) and a current supporter of the National Unity Platform (NUP) political party.

propositions.text: He claims to have supported political figures financially since 2010 and became more active with NUP and People Power Movement when his friend entered politics.
propositions.quote: He claims that he has supported various political figures financially since 2010 and that he became more actively involved with the NUP and the People Power Movement when his friend, XXXX XXXX, entered politics.

propositions.text: He claims he was arrested with other opposition supporters in 2020 and that armed men broke into his home in 2021, after which he escaped and went into hiding and relocated his family.
propositions.quote: He claims that he was arrested along with other opposition party supporters on XXXX XXXX, 2020, and that armed men in military trousers broke into his home on XXXX XXXX, 2021. He explains that he managed to escape and went into hiding and that he also relocated his family.

propositions.text: An agent arranged for him to receive a Canadian travel visa and informed him he could travel in 2022; he arrived in Canada and requested protection shortly thereafter.
propositions.quote: He explains that an agent arranged for him to receive a Canadian travel visa and that the agent informed him that he could travel in XXXX 2022. The Appellant arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2022, and requested protection shortly thereafter.

propositions.text: The RPD concluded the Appellant is not credible due to inconsistencies about his NUP membership and mistreatment, and unreliable supporting documents.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) concluded that the Appellant is not a credible witness due to multiple inconsistencies relating to his membership in the NUP and the resulting mistreatment, and the unreliability of documentation provided to support his claim.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD incorrectly considered documentary evidence, failed to consider his testimony about arrest and torture, disregarded delay explanations, and speculated about targeting due to Canadian NUP membership.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD incorrectly considered objective and personal documentary evidence that supports his claims, failed to consider his own testimony about being arrested and failed to ask him about incidents of torture that he experienced in Uganda, disregarded statements in his narrative that explain a delay in leaving Uganda, and speculated that he would not be targeted in Uganda due to his membership in the Canadian NUP chapter.

propositions.text: The determinative issue on appeal is the credibility of the claim.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue on appeal is the credibility of the claim.

propositions.text: The Appellant has not established the credibility of the basis of his claim; his testimony is vague, contradictory, or unsupported by evidence.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has not established the credibility of the basis of his claim (BOC). The Appellant's testimony about his political activities in Uganda is vague, contradictory, or unsupported by documentary evidence.

propositions.text: Letters from witnesses in Uganda contradict his political activity allegations and circumstances leading authorities to pursue him.
propositions.quote: Letters from witnesses in Uganda contradict his allegations about his political activities in Uganda and the circumstances allegedly leading the authorities in Uganda to pursue him.

propositions.text: The Appellant's explanations for inconsistencies are insufficient to overcome credibility concerns.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's explanations for those inconsistencies are insufficient to overcome the credibility concerns that have been identified.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal, summarizes the Appellant's claims and history, notes the RPD found him not credible due to inconsistencies, and finds the Appellant failed to establish credibility.

propositions.text: I dismiss the appeal and find the RPD was correct that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal. The RPD was correct in finding that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and agrees with the RPD's finding that the Appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant requested the RAD admit new evidence on appeal, submitted requests at perfection and after, and requested an oral hearing arguing new evidence rebuts RPD findings and addresses credibility.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has requested that the RAD admit new evidence on appeal. The Appellant submitted new evidence requests, both at the time of perfection and after perfecting his appeal. The Appellant has also requested an oral hearing arguing that the new evidence clearly rebuts most of the RPD's findings and specifically addresses the issue of his credibility.

propositions.text: The evidence presented by the Appellant is accepted in part.
propositions.quote: The evidence presented by the Appellant is accepted, in part

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Appellant's requests to admit new evidence and for an oral hearing, and accepts some of the evidence presented.

propositions.text: The Appellant requested admission of a Statutory Declaration from his wife and her identification, and a letter from a clinic summarizing his treatment, as new evidence at perfection.
propositions.quote: The Appellant requested that the following be admitted as new evidence at the time of perfection. a. A Statutory Declaration from the Appellant's wife, dated XXXX XXXX, 2023, and her identification; b. A letter from a XXXX at the XXXX XXXX Clinic summarizing the Appellant's treatment, dated XXXX XXXX, 2023.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant requested admission of his wife's statutory declaration and a clinic letter summarizing his treatment as new evidence at perfection.

propositions.text: On August 15, 2023, the Appellant requested admission of a statutory declaration from his wife and a copy of Release on Bond issued by Uganda Police as new evidence after perfection.
propositions.quote: On August 15, 2023, the Appellant requested that the following be admitted as new evidence, therefore after perfection: (i) A Statutory Declaration from the Appellant's wife, dated XXXX XXXX, 2023, along with her identification; (ii) Copy of Release on Bond, issued by the Uganda Police for "XXXX XXXX XXXX", dated XXXX XXXX, 2023.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant requested admission of his wife's statutory declaration and a Release on Bond document as new evidence after perfection.

propositions.text: The RAD can only accept evidence that arose after the RPD decision, was not reasonably available at the time, or could not reasonably have been brought before the RPD.
propositions.quote: According to the Law,1 I can only accept evidence that: (iii) arose after the RPD decision; or (iv) was not reasonably available at the time of the decision; or (v) that the Appellant could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to bring to the RPD before the decision.

propositions.text: If evidence meets these requirements, the RAD must decide if it is new, credible, and relevant before acceptance.
propositions.quote: (vi) If the evidence meets one or more of these requirements, I must decide if the evidence is new, credible, and relevant before I can accept it.

propositions.text: If new evidence is requested after perfection, the RAD must also consider relevance, probative value, and whether the Appellant could have provided it at perfection.
propositions.quote: (vii) In addition, if the request to admit new evidence occurs after perfection, the RAD must also consider the documents relevance and probative value, and the new evidence that the documents bring to the appeal, and whether the Appellant could have provided the documents at the time of perfection.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the legal criteria for admitting new evidence on appeal, including timing, availability, credibility, relevance, and probative value.

propositions.text: The statutory declaration from the Appellant's wife does not meet IRPA Section 110(4) requirements as it repeats information already available to the RPD.
propositions.quote: The Statutory Declaration from the Appellant's wife, dated XXXX XXXX, 2023, does not meet the requirements set out in Section 110(4) in the Immigration Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). The declaration simply repeats information stated in the Appellant's BOC. This information was available to the RPD before it submitted its decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the wife's statutory declaration inadmissible as new evidence because it repeats information already before the RPD.

propositions.text: The letter from the Appellant's clinic is accepted as new evidence as it is dated after the RPD decision and credible.
propositions.quote: The letter from the Appellant's XXXX is accepted as new evidence. It is dated XXXX XXXX, 2023, and indicates that he has been undertaking XXXX treatments since XXXX 2023, after the RPD issued its decision. This information is new because it is not part of the RPD record. I accept that the letter is credible in that it was prepared by a registered XXXX.

propositions.text: Information related to the Appellant's state of mind is relevant to credibility questions.
propositions.quote: Information related to the Appellant's state of mind is relevant to questions of credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts the clinic letter as new, credible, and relevant evidence related to the Appellant's state of mind and credibility.

propositions.text: The wife's statutory declaration and Release on Bond are not admitted as new evidence due to credibility concerns and convenience.
propositions.quote: The Statutory Declaration from the Appellant's wife and the copy of the Release on Bond are not admitted as new evidence. I find that this evidence is too convenient to be credible.

propositions.text: The wife's return to Uganda and alleged arrest after the claim was rejected is likely fabricated to remedy credibility problems.
propositions.quote: It is more likely than not that this arrest was fabricated in order to remedy the credibility problems inherent to the Appellant's claim.

propositions.text: On balance, the wife would not return to a location where she was allegedly being sought if the Appellant's claims were credible.
propositions.quote: On a balance of probabilities, the Appellant's wife would not return to a location where she was allegedly being told that people are regularly coming around in search of the Appellant if his claims of harm were credible.

propositions.text: The Release on Bond document has credibility problems: seal not fully visible, no officer signature, and inconsistencies about court appearances.
propositions.quote: Additionally, the Release on Bond document contains credibility problems. The document's seal is not fully visible. The document is not signed by the officer who would have completed the release on bond. The document is dated XXXX XXXX, 2023, and indicates that the Appellant's wife was to appear in court on XXXX XXXX, 2023. In the Statutory Declaration dated XXXX XXXX, 2023, the Appellant's wife does not indicate that she appeared in court or failed to appear in court, for example, because she is in hiding, or whether she has been reporting to the XXXX Central station every 10 days as claimed in the declaration.

propositions.text: The late new evidence documents are not credible.
propositions.quote: The documents that are part of the late request for new evidence are not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the wife's declaration and Release on Bond as new evidence due to credibility issues and likely fabrication to fix credibility problems.

propositions.text: The rejected new evidence does not address the RPD's credibility concerns about NUP membership and arrest circumstances.
propositions.quote: I also find that the documents that I am not accepting as new evidence do not speak to the credibility concerns raised by the RPD, which go to the heart of whether the Appellant was a member of the NUP in Uganda and the circumstances of the alleged arrest by police.

propositions.text: These statements presume the claim's credibility and address prospective risk, not the primary determinative issue of political activity credibility.
propositions.quote: These statements and documents presume that the credibility of the basis of the claim has been established and speak to the prospective risk of harm related to an ongoing interest that the Ugandan authorities would have in the Appellant. They do not serve to establish the credibility of the Appellant's political activities in Uganda and therefore they are not relevant to the primary determinative issue.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the rejected new evidence irrelevant to the primary issue of the Appellant's political activity credibility and the circumstances of arrest.

propositions.text: Since only the clinic letter is accepted and it does not address credibility issues, an oral hearing is unnecessary.
propositions.quote: Given that I have only accepted the XXXX letter on appeal, which does not speak to the credibility issues that are determinative of the claim, it is not necessary to hold an oral hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes an oral hearing is unnecessary as accepted new evidence does not address credibility issues.

propositions.text: My role is to consider all evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.4 Credibility

paragraphs.summary: The court states its role is to review all evidence and determine if the RPD decision was correct.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant alleges targeting due to NUP membership and mobilization but was not a member in Uganda and found inconsistencies in testimony and documents.
propositions.quote: The RPD determined that though the Appellant alleges that he is targeted by the Ugandan government and security forces due to his membership in the NUP and his mobilization work on their behalf, he was not a member of the NUP in Uganda. It found that testimony and personal documents submitted to support his claim are inconsistent with the Appellant's Basis of Claim form (BOC) narrative.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant was not a NUP member in Uganda and that his testimony and documents were inconsistent with his claim.

propositions.text: After reviewing the hearing and evidence, I find the Appellant has not established his claim on a balance of probabilities, including NUP membership and mobilizer profile.
propositions.quote: After listening to the hearing recording and considering all of the evidence before me, I find that the Appellant has not established the basis of his claim on a balance of probabilities. The Appellant has not established his membership in the NUP, in Uganda, or his profile as a NUP mobilizer

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant has not proven his NUP membership or mobilizer role on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: The Appellant claims he joined the NUP on XXXX XXXX, 2020, in Uganda.
propositions.quote: The Appellant claims that he joined the NUP on XXXX XXXX, 2020, in XXXX, Uganda.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant claims he joined the NUP in Uganda in 2020.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant could describe the NUP's objectives broadly but his knowledge was not consistent with his alleged profile as a supporter since 2017 and member since 2020.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant could describe the NUP's party objective in broad terms but that his level of knowledge was not commensurate with his alleged profile as a supporter of the People Power Movement since 2017 and a party member since 2020.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's knowledge of the NUP was too limited for his claimed profile and membership duration.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by not clarifying roles in the NUP, failing to ask about slogans, and not considering his education and background.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD did not provide clear reasons for its finding that his knowledge and engagement with the NUP was minimal. He submits that the RPD only asked a general question about the NUP "and did not make any difference and thus, clarifications between the roles in the NUP as a political party."5 He submits that he testified, in a straightforward manner, that he was mobilizing by encouraging people to register their national identity cards and vote, and to support the party and remove the dictator, indicating that he was more of a supporter and an NUP member in the field who was not attending meetings. He argues that the RPD did not ask further questions to clarify whether there were differences between members whose role was to mobilize the people and members who were within the NUP leadership structure. He argues that the RPD further erred by failing to ask further questions about the NUP's slogans while only relying upon one general slogan and that the RPD did not consider his education and personal background when assessing his knowledge of the party.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by not clarifying NUP roles, not asking about slogans, and ignoring his education and background.

propositions.text: The RPD asked several questions about political involvement; the Appellant could not answer detailed questions or about the party slogan, which was on submitted evidence.
propositions.quote: The RPD asked several questions about the Appellant's political involvement. The Appellant could not answer any detailed questions about his local NUP chapter's structure and testified that he was not able to attend any party meetings at the local chapter. The RPD asked the Appellant what is the NUP's slogan, and he could not answer that simple question, though the slogan is printed on a letter from the NUP that he submitted as part of his evidence.6

propositions.text: The RPD was not required to coax correct answers; a self-described important mobilizer should know the party slogan.
propositions.quote: The RPD was not required to continue to ask the Appellant questions in order to coax the correct answer from him. The Appellant is a self-described important mobilizer within the NUP who is close to party leadership. Knowing the party slogan does not require any particular educational background. It was correct of the RPD to find that a party mobilizer in the field would know the party slogan.

propositions.text: The Appellant's inability to answer simple questions about the NUP undermines his credibility and claim of being sought as a political dissident.
propositions.quote: His inability to answer simple questions about the NUP calls into question the credibility of his engagement with the party and the claim that he is sought out as a political dissident.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's inability to answer questions about the NUP slogan undermines his credibility as a political mobilizer.

propositions.text: The Appellant's connection to NUP appears limited to friendship and donations; contradictions prevent establishing a larger mobilizer role or local chapter membership.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's connection to the NUP party and its predecessor, the People Party Movement, appears to be that he was a personal friend of an MP and of XXXX XXXX , and that he made donations as a local business owner. Contradictions in his evidence are such that he has not established that he played a larger role as a mobilizer in the field, on a balance of probabilities. The Appellant has not established that he was a member of the NUP's XXXX chapter

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's connection to NUP limited to friendship and donations, with contradictions preventing proof of a larger role or chapter membership.

propositions.text: The Appellant provided a letter from the NUP's XXXX chapter with his Toronto membership number, but he claims local chapter membership and police confiscation of local membership card.
propositions.quote: The Appellant provided the RPD with a letter from the NUP's XXXX chapter.7 That letter contains the Appellant's Toronto NUP membership number though he claims to have been a member of the local chapter before leaving Uganda and testified that the police confiscated his NUP XXXX chapter membership card when he was arrested.

propositions.text: The RPD questioned why the letter included Toronto membership number instead of local chapter number; the Appellant claimed a break-in deleted local records but had no evidence for this.
propositions.quote: The RPD asked the Appellant why the XXXX chapter would include his Toronto membership number instead of a local chapter number to confirm his membership. The Appellant testified that the XXXX offices had been broken into and that those people stole documents and deleted information in the system. When further questioned about the break in, the Appellant admitted that he had no evidence to establish the incident and that he was speculating.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's evidence about local NUP membership contradicted by a letter with Toronto membership number and unsupported break-in claim.

propositions.text: RPD erred by not considering letter came from third party and was arranged through an agent
propositions.quote: the Appellant argues that the RPD erred because it did not take into account that the letter was coming from a third party and that he arranged for the letter to arrive through an agent

propositions.text: Appellant's argument amplifies problems with the letter and does not explain invented break to resolve letter issues
propositions.quote: I do not accept the Appellant's argument and find that it amplifies rather than resolves the problems with the letter. His argument on appeal does not explain why he invented a break in in order to explain the problems with the letter

propositions.text: Inventing incident to resolve credibility concern detracts from Appellant's overall credibility
propositions.quote: I find that his impulse to invent an incident to resolve a credibility concern detracts from his overall credibility

propositions.text: Appellant's explanation about arranging letter through agent detracts from letter's credibility
propositions.quote: The Appellant's explanation that he arranged for the letter through an agent also detracts from its credibility because he cannot testify to how the letter was obtained from the chapter or its authenticity

propositions.text: Sending NUP Toronto membership info detracts from credibility of claim of prior party membership in Uganda
propositions.quote: His explanation that he sent them his NUP Toronto membership information so that the letter could be produced detracts from the credibility of the claim that he was previously a member of the party in Uganda

propositions.text: Appellant's response to RPD's concern about letter detracts from credibility of his membership and being sought in Uganda
propositions.quote: Like the RPD, I find that the Appellant's response to the RPD's concern about the NUP XXXX chapter's letter detracts from the credibility of his assertion that he was a member of the NUP in Uganda and that he is sought out in Uganda for this reason

propositions.text: RPD did not err by assigning no weight to the letter
propositions.quote: The RPD did not err by assigning no weight to the letter

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred on the letter's origin; the court finds the argument amplifies problems and detracts from credibility, supporting RPD's no weight assignment.

propositions.text: Appellant has not established NUP XXXX chapter membership on balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant has not established his membership in the NUP's XXXX chapter on a balance of probabilities

propositions.text: Letter's reference to Toronto membership number and 'foot soldier' term call its credibility into question
propositions.quote: The XXXX chapter's letter reference to the NUP Toronto membership number and its reference to the Appellant as a foot soldier call into question its credibility

propositions.text: Appellant testified 'foot soldier' means door-to-door explaining party ideas but could not recall NUP slogan
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified that a foot soldier is one who moves on foot going door to door explaining the party's ideas and objectives, yet he was unable to recall a basic detail about the NUP's slogan

propositions.text: Letter calls Appellant a 'big fish' but he testified he does not know leaders and missed meetings
propositions.quote: The letter refers to the Appellant as big fish of the NUP, yet he testified that he does not know who are the leaders taking the lead in the XXXX chapter, and that he was not able to attend meetings with the chairman and the MP, who recruited him to politics, because in those times, he was running up and down

propositions.text: Appellant's testimony contradicts letter's characterization as 'big fish'
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant's testimony contradicts the letter's characterization of his profile as a big fish

propositions.text: Problems with letter and other witness letters cause conclusion that Appellant's political profile and activities lack credibility
propositions.quote: The problems with the letter, together with credibility concerns identified in other letters from alleged witnesses, cause me to conclude that he has not established the credibility of his political profile or activities in Uganda

propositions.text: Appellant has not established mistreatment by authorities on balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: The Appellant has not established that he was mistreated by authorities in Uganda on a balance of probabilities

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant failed to prove NUP membership and political profile credibility, noting contradictions and letter issues, and no mistreatment established.

propositions.text: RPD concluded alleged mistreatment by Ugandan government did not happen due to inconsistent corroborating evidence
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that alleged mistreatment by the Ugandan government did not happen due to evidence submitted to corroborate his allegations that are inconsistent with his BOC narrative

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found alleged mistreatment did not occur due to inconsistent corroborating evidence with the appellant's narrative.

propositions.text: Letter from friend KS indicates appellant was arrested and tortured in 2020
propositions.quote: A letter of support from a friend, KS8, indicates that the Appellant was arrested in 2020 and tortured by the police during his detention

propositions.text: Appellant's BOC omits mention of torture; he said BOC was brief summary
propositions.quote: The Appellant's BOC omits any mention of being tortured. When asked about the omission, the Appellant responded that he only put down a brief summary in his BOC

propositions.text: Appellant said friend knew about torture because friend was arrested at same time
propositions.quote: When asked how his friend knew about the torture, the Appellant responded that his friend was arrested at the same time

propositions.text: Appellant did not know why friend did not mention being arrested at same time in letter
propositions.quote: When asked why his friend did not mention being arrested at the same time in his letter, the Appellant did not know why

propositions.text: RPD placed low weight on friend's letter and drew negative inference from omission in BOC
propositions.quote: The RPD placed low weight on the friend's letter and drew a negative inference about the omission from the Appellant's BOC

paragraphs.summary: Friend's letter alleges arrest and torture; appellant's BOC omits torture; RPD gave low weight to letter and drew negative inference.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred by not asking specific questions about torture or witnessing torture
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD erred because it did not ask specific questions about whether he was actually tortured or witnessed the torture of others who were arrested with him

propositions.text: Appellant relies on friend's letter stating friend 'was aware' of his arrest
propositions.quote: He relies upon a statement in his friend's letter indicating that his friend "was aware" of his arrest

propositions.text: Appellant adds objective evidence shows Ugandan authorities arrested opposition and restricted media
propositions.quote: He adds that the objective evidence on Uganda indicates that authorities broke up opposition rallies, arrested government critics and opposition members, and placed restrictions on the media

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by not probing torture details and cites friend's letter and objective evidence of government repression.

propositions.text: RPD correctly detracted from credibility due to omission from BOC
propositions.quote: I do not accept the Appellant's arguments and find that the RPD correctly detracted from his credibility due to the omission from his BOC

propositions.text: RPD asked appellant to fill in arrest details but testimony was vague and general
propositions.quote: The RPD asked the Appellant what happened when he was arrested and specifically asked him to fill in the details. The Appellant's testimony about his arrest was vague and contained very general information

propositions.text: Appellant's vague testimony about arrest detracts from credibility of claim he was arrested in XXXX 2020
propositions.quote: I find this testimony to be very vague and general, and I detract from the credibility of the claim that he was arrested in XXXX 2020

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD rightly detracted credibility due to BOC omission and vague arrest testimony, undermining arrest claim credibility.

propositions.text: Friend's statement about awareness does not resolve RPD's credibility concerns
propositions.quote: I find that his friend's statement about being aware of the Appellant's problems does not resolve the credibility concerns that the RPD raised

propositions.text: Letter's mention of torture not alleged in BOC and omission of friend's arrest diminish letter's credibility and probative value
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that the letter's credibility and probative value is diminished by the mention of torture that the Appellant did not allege in his BOC and by the omission of the friend's alleged arrest, as claimed by the Appellant in his oral testimony

propositions.text: Inconsistencies lead to assigning no weight to the letter
propositions.quote: These inconsistencies lead me to assign no weight to the letter

propositions.text: Letter is inconsistent with appellant's claims and explanations worsen inconsistencies
propositions.quote: The letter is inconsistent with the Appellant's claims and the Appellant's explanations further exacerbate those inconsistencies

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the friend's letter inconsistent with appellant's claims and assigns it no weight due to contradictions and omissions.

propositions.text: RPD found letter from friend MD not credible due to inconsistencies with appellant's claims
propositions.quote: The RPD found that a letter from a friend, MD9, not to be credible. In the letter, MD claims to be aware that the Appellant has been imprisoned several times and received death threats. The Appellant only alleges that he was detained once

propositions.text: Appellant testified he does not know why letter says several imprisonments and that he and MD were arrested together
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified that he does not know why the letter indicates that he was imprisoned several times, and that he and MD were arrested together

propositions.text: Appellant does not know why MD's letter omits that MD was arrested with him
propositions.quote: When asked why MD does not indicate that he was arrested with the Appellant, the Appellant responded that he did not know why

propositions.text: RPD did not find appellant's explanations reasonable and placed low weight on MD's letter
propositions.quote: The RPD did not find the Appellant's explanations to be reasonable and placed low weight on the letter

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found MD's letter not credible due to inconsistencies; appellant's explanations were unreasonable; low weight assigned to letter.

propositions.text: Appellant argues documents corroborating some story aspects should not be discounted for not corroborating others
propositions.quote: On appeal, the Appellant argues that documents that corroborate some aspects of a person's story cannot be discounted merely because they do not corroborate other aspects of a story or provide sufficient detail

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD erred by not considering his testimony of arrest and objective evidence of opposition arrests
propositions.quote: He submits that the RPD erred because it did not consider the Appellant's testimony that he was arrested and repeats the argument relating to objective evidence indicating that opposition members are arrested by government authorities

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues documents corroborating some story parts should not be discounted and that RPD erred by ignoring his arrest testimony and objective evidence.

propositions.text: Argument about discounting documents does not apply to appellant's evidence
propositions.quote: While I agree that in some cases a document that corroborates some aspects of a person's story should not be discounted when it does not corroborate other aspects of the story, I find that this argument does not apply to the Appellant's documentary evidence

propositions.text: Letters from MD and KS contradict appellant's allegations and are unreliable
propositions.quote: The problem with the letters from MD and KS is that they directly contradict the Appellant's allegations. MD's letter speaks of several imprisonments where the claim is that there was one detention. This inconsistency renders MD's claim that he is aware of the Appellant's story unreliable

propositions.text: MD has not corroborated appellant's claims with credible testimony
propositions.quote: MD has not corroborated the Appellant's claims with credible testimony

propositions.text: Appellant's claim of arrest with MD and KS is not corroborated by either affiant
propositions.quote: The Appellant's claim that he was arrested with MD and KS is not corroborated by either affiant

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's argument inapplicable; letters from MD and KS contradict and do not credibly corroborate appellant's claims.

propositions.text: KS's letter conflicts with appellant's narrative about political involvement and party membership
propositions.quote: I note that the letter from KS indicates that he personally involved the Appellant in politics as a mobilizer in 2010 whereas the Appellant's narrative indicates that BN approached him and requested that he support her campaign while she was a member of the Democratic Party (DP)

propositions.text: KS claims joint DP membership in youth contradicts appellant's testimony of joining DP in 2017
propositions.quote: KS also claims that he was a member of the DP with the Appellant when they were youths. The Appellant's narrative does not mention being a DP member in his youth. The Appellant testified that he joined the DP in 2017

propositions.text: Appellant's narrative and testimony contradict KS's testimony
propositions.quote: The Appellant's narrative and testimony contradicts KS's testimony

propositions.text: This contradiction is an additional reason to assign no weight to KS's letter for corroboration
propositions.quote: I find that this is an additional reason to assign no weight to KS's letter for the purposes of corroborating the Appellant's claim

paragraphs.summary: The court finds KS's letter contradicts appellant's narrative and testimony, justifying no weight assigned to KS's letter for corroboration.

propositions.text: KS and MD state awareness of appellant's arrest and flight but do not explain how they know
propositions.quote: Both KS and MD state that they are aware that the Appellant was arrested and that he fled to Canada after being threatened. However, neither affiant explained how they became aware of these facts

propositions.text: Neither affiant credibly speaks to appellant's sole alleged arrest or claims of joint arrest
propositions.quote: Given that neither affiant was able to credibly speak to the Appellant's sole alleged arrest and given that neither affiant declared being arrested along with the Appellant as he claims that they were, I find that they are not credible witnesses to the Appellant's alleged troubles

paragraphs.summary: The court finds KS and MD do not credibly explain their knowledge of appellant's arrest and are not credible witnesses to his troubles.

propositions.text: Letters from MD and KS are assigned no weight regarding appellant's detention by authorities
propositions.quote: It is for all of these reasons that I assign no weight to the letters from MD and KS with respect to establishing that the Appellant was detained by government authorities in Uganda because he is an opposition party member or because he opposes government policies or practices

propositions.text: Appellant submitted letters contradicting his claims and did not know why affiants omitted relevant info, detracting from his credibility
propositions.quote: Moreover, it is the Appellant who submitted letters that contradict his claims and who responded that he does not know why his affiants did or did not include relevant information in their letters, and this detracts from his own credibility

paragraphs.summary: The court assigns no weight to MD and KS letters and finds appellant's submission of contradictory letters and ignorance detracts from his credibility.

propositions.text: Mentions of opposition mistreatment in Uganda's NDP do not establish appellant's own mistreatment on balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: Mentions of mistreatment of opposition members in the National Documentation Package (NDP) for Uganda do not establish the Appellant's own claims of mistreatment, on a balance of probabilities

propositions.text: Others' problems in Uganda do not establish appellant's political activities or resolve contradictions in his claim
propositions.quote: The fact that others in Uganda have experienced problems does not establish the Appellant's own political activities on a balance of probabilities and does not do away with the contradictions and the inconsistencies in the Appellant's own claim and testimony

paragraphs.summary: The court finds general opposition mistreatment evidence does not establish appellant's mistreatment or resolve his claim contradictions.

propositions.text: Appellant does not respond to each RPD conclusion on other documentation but says KS and MD letter arguments apply
propositions.quote: On appeal, the Appellant does not respond to each of the RPD's conclusions about other documentation that he submitted in support of his claim. Rather, he submits that the arguments relating to the letters from KS and MD also apply to these conclusions

propositions.text: Appellant's argument insufficient to overcome RPD concerns; court supports RPD's conclusion of insufficient evidence
propositions.quote: I find that this argument is insufficient to overcome the concerns identified by the RPD. My own examination leads me to support the RPD's conclusion that the evidence is insufficient to establish the credibility of the basis of the claim

propositions.text: Court notes additional problems with some evidence adding to RPD's credibility concerns
propositions.quote: Additionally, I have noted the following problems with some of this evidence that add to the RPD's credibility concerns

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's general argument insufficient and supports RPD's conclusion of insufficient credible evidence, noting further problems.

propositions.text: Letter from KI alleges youths and association members arrested, tortured, killed due to association with appellant
propositions.quote: A letter from KI10 contains an allegation that was omitted from the Appellant's BOC. KI's letter states that many youths and members of his association were arrested, tortured and killed because of their close association with the Appellant

propositions.text: Appellant did not make KI's claim in testimony; letter is unreliable and assigned no weight
propositions.quote: The Appellant did not make this claim in his oral or written testimony. Considering that other letters from alleged witnesses also contain allegations that are not part of the Appellant's BOC or his oral testimony, I find that this letter is not reliable, and I assign it no weight with respect to establishing or corroborating the Appellant's claim

paragraphs.summary: The court finds KI's letter contains unalleged claims omitted by appellant and assigns it no weight as unreliable evidence.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges close friendships with BN and XXXX XXXX since 2010 and 2008, main political contacts
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that he has close friendships with BN and with XXXX XXXX. He alleges that he has known BN since at least 2010 and XXXX XXXX since at least 2008

propositions.text: BN and XXXX XXXX invited appellant into politics; association main reason he is sought in Uganda
propositions.quote: In his story, they are the main people who invite him into politics within the DP and NUP parties, and his association with them is the main reason why he is allegedly sought out in Uganda

propositions.text: Court does not accept appellant's explanation that BN and XXXX XXXX are too sick or busy to provide corroboration
propositions.quote: I do not accept the Appellant's explanations that BN and XXXX XXXX are too sick or too busy to provide him with corroboration

propositions.text: Appellant did not attempt to contact BN and XXXX XXXX; this detracts from credibility given contradictions
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified that he did not attempt to contact them for these reasons, not that he was told by them or their representatives that they could not provide him with letters. Given the contradictions and inconsistencies in his evidence, I detract from the credibility of his claim because he did not attempt to obtain corroboration from these two people

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's claimed political contacts uncorroborated and his failure to seek corroboration detracts from credibility.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred finding five-month delay in leaving Uganda indicates lack of subjective fear
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD erred by finding that his delay of five months living in Uganda before leaving the country indicates a lack of subjective fear

propositions.text: Appellant cites BOC that agent helped secure visa but advised waiting; agent informed travel possible only in XXXX 2022
propositions.quote: He cites his BOC, indicating that an agent helped him to secure a Canadian visa but later advised him to wait while he searched for another purpose of travel and that the agent informed him only in XXXX 2022 that he can travel

propositions.text: Appellant's BOC indicates he was hiding and workers informed him people were coming around
propositions.quote: He adds that his BOC indicates that he was hiding in the meantime and that workers informed him that people were coming around

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred on delay indicating fear, citing agent's advice and his hiding during the wait.

propositions.text: RPD correctly concluded delay between visa receipt and departure detracts from subjective fear
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD correctly concluded that the Appellant's decision to remain in Uganda between receiving his travel visa in XXXX 2021 and his departure in XXXX 2022 detracts from a subjective fear of harm

propositions.text: Delay alone not determinative but appellant had visa and did not leave immediately despite claiming active threats
propositions.quote: While the delay alone is not determinative, the Appellant claims that he was actively sought out and that those who threaten him were visiting his home. The Appellant had a travel visa allowing him to leave Uganda immediately and did not

propositions.text: Court rejects appellant's explanation of travel timing; evidence shows intention to travel in XXXX 2022
propositions.quote: I do not accept the Appellant's explanation that he was later told that he could travel in XXXX 2022. His Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) application indicates that he always intended to travel in XXXX 2022

propositions.text: TRV application signed in XXXX 2021 indicates XXXX 2022 travel date
propositions.quote: The Application was signed on XXXX XXXX, 2021. The XXXX 2022 travel date is indicated in a letter dated XXXX XXXX, 2021, and signed by the Appellant

propositions.text: Evidence indicates intention to travel in XXXX 2022, so no subjective fear between XXXX 2021 and XXXX 2022
propositions.quote: The evidence before me indicates that the intention was always to travel in XXXX 2022, which leads me to conclude that he did not subjectively fear harm in the period of time between XXXX 2021 and XXXX 2022

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the delay detracts from subjective fear, rejecting appellant's explanation and concluding no fear between visa receipt and travel.

propositions.text: Appellant's BOC claim of hiding from XXXX 2021 creates credibility concern about remaining in Uganda despite visa
propositions.quote: His BOC indicates that he was hiding as of XXXX 2021. This claim creates an additional credibility concern related to why he remained in Uganda in hiding for more than a year despite receiving a travel visa in XXXX 2021

propositions.text: Inconsistency between alleged fear and behavior detracts from credibility and indicates lack of subjective fear
propositions.quote: This inconsistency between his alleged fear and his allegations further causes me to detract from the credibility of the claim and to conclude that his behaviour is indicative of a lack of subjective fear of harm

propositions.text: Appellant's mental health condition does not explain contradictions and inconsistencies detracting from credibility
propositions.quote: The Appellant's mental health condition does not explain the contradictions and the inconsistencies that detract from the credibility of his claim

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's hiding claim inconsistent with behavior, detracting credibility and not explained by mental health.

propositions.text: RPD erred by not asking about mental health when doubting credibility
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD erred because it did not ask any questions about his mental health and condition when it started to doubt his credibility.

propositions.text: Counsel also did not raise mental health issues at RPD
propositions.quote: The Appellant acknowledges that Counsel also did not raise these issues at the RPD.

propositions.text: No evidence at RPD suggested mental health concerns affecting testimony
propositions.quote: There was no evidence presented to the RPD suggesting that the Appellant was suffering from any mental health concerns that would affect his ability to testify.

propositions.text: Evidence to RAD does not explain credibility problems identified
propositions.quote: The evidence presented to the RAD on appeal also does not suggest anything that would explain the numerous credibility problems identified in the RPD's decision or in this decision.

propositions.text: Letter from XXXX indicates illness but lacks explanation or impact on testimony
propositions.quote: A letter from his XXXX12 indicates only that he is suffering from XXXX and XXXX without explaining how the XXXX arrived at this conclusion and without indicating how his condition could impact his testimony.

propositions.text: Letter insufficient to establish mental health caused inconsistencies or lack of credibility
propositions.quote: This letter is insufficient to establish that mental health concerns are responsible for any inconsistencies or a lack of credible testimony.

propositions.text: Appellant has not established credibility of basis of his claim
propositions.quote: The Appellant has not established the credibility of the basis of his claim

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RPD erred by not questioning mental health; no evidence showed mental health issues affecting testimony; letter insufficient; court finds appellant not credible.

propositions.text: Objective evidence shows politically active NUP supporters in Uganda face government oppression
propositions.quote: The objective evidence on the treatment of NUP supporters does indicate that those who are politically active supporters of the NUP in Uganda can face government oppression.

propositions.text: Targeted supporters include NUP president, MPs, polling station employees, election observers, protesters
propositions.quote: Supporters who have been targeted include the NUP's president, MPs, polling station employees, election observers, and active protesters.

propositions.text: Contradictions mean appellant has not established credible political profile subjecting him to oppression
propositions.quote: The contradictions identified in the RPD's decision and in this decision mean that the Appellant has not established the credibility of his claim that he had a political profile that would subject him to government oppression.

propositions.text: Appellant lacks expected knowledge of party as active mobilizer
propositions.quote: He has not established that he has knowledge of the party that one might reasonably expect of an active party mobilizer.

propositions.text: Appellant has not credibly explained why letter only refers to Toronto NUP membership number
propositions.quote: He has not credibly explained why the letter from the XXXX chapter only refers to his Toronto NUP membership number.

propositions.text: Supporting documentation contradicts appellant's testimony about political activities and arrest
propositions.quote: His supporting documentation contradicts his own testimony about the nature of his political activities and his arrest in Uganda.

propositions.text: Contradictions lead to conclusion appellant has not established political profile, arrest, or being sought by authorities on balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: Taken together, these contradictions cause me to conclude that he has not established his political profile on a balance of probabilities, that he was arrested in XXXX 2020 on a balance of probabilities, or that he is sought out by authorities in Uganda.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds objective evidence shows NUP supporters face oppression but appellant's contradictions undermine his political profile and arrest claims.

propositions.text: RPD did not err in finding appellant failed to establish credible sur place claim related to Toronto NUP membership
propositions.quote: The RPD did not err in finding that the Appellant has not established the credibility of a sur place claim related to his membership in the NUP's Toronto chapter.

propositions.text: Appellant's appeal arguments unclear and do not respond to RPD's conclusions about political participation in Canada
propositions.quote: The Appellant's appeal arguments are unclear and do not respond to the specific conclusions that the RPD made in its decision about his political participation in Canada: The panel erred when concluded that the Appellant's membership in NUP Toronto chapter was to have garnered the attention of Ugandan authorities or made him a target of the government as this finding by the panel is made on speculations, taken into account the previous statement made by the panel that in the NDP there was no evidence indicating that the Ugandan government is known for tracking NUP members in foreign jurisdictions.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD did not err rejecting sur place claim; appellant's appeal arguments unclear and unresponsive to RPD findings.

propositions.text: RPD accepted appellant joined Toronto NUP chapter in XXXX 2022 but found limited involvement insufficient for serious persecution possibility
propositions.quote: The RPD accepted that the Appellant joined the NUP's Toronto chapter in XXXX 2022 but found that given his limited implication, his membership in that chapter is insufficient to establish a serious possibility of persecution in Uganda.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found appellant's limited involvement in Toronto NUP insufficient to establish serious persecution possibility.

propositions.text: RPD's determination correct: appellant attended only three meetings, no official responsibilities, no vocal criticism or political activity on social media
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD's determination is correct. The RPD noted that the Appellant only attended three meetings with the Toronto chapter, that he has not taken on any official responsibilities with the Toronto NUP, and that there was no evidence that he has been vocally critical of the Ugandan government or that he has been politically active on social media.

propositions.text: RPD correctly considered appellant's testimony on political activities in Canada
propositions.quote: The RPD correctly considered the Appellant's testimony on this issue.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD's determination correct about appellant's limited political activity and proper consideration of testimony.

propositions.text: RPD correctly characterized appellant's political activities in Canada
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD has correctly characterized the Appellant's political activities in Canada.

propositions.text: Joining Toronto NUP and attending three meetings does not establish political profile targeted by Ugandan government
propositions.quote: I find that joining the Toronto NUP and passively attending three meetings does not establish that the Appellant has a political profile that establishes him to be an opposition critic that the Ugandan government would take note of or track in a foreign jurisdiction leading him to be targeted in Uganda.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD correctly characterized appellant's political activities as insufficient to establish targeting risk.

propositions.text: Dismiss appeal and confirm RPD decision that appellant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses appeal and confirms RPD decision denying refugee or protection status.
